Boil The Breakfast Early

“Boil The Breakfast Early” is related to an old Highland reel found in Captain Fraser’s 1816 collection:

X: 1
T: Fashion Which the Lasses Have, The
T: Am fasan th’aig na Caileagan
S: Airs & Melodies Peculiar to the Highlands of Scotland…
N:Transposed from A major for comparison
Z: Nigel Gatherer
M: 4/4
L: 1/8
K: G
B | GE E/E/E GDDB | GE E/E/E B2 AB | GE E/E/E GDDG | EFGA B3 :|
e | dGeG BAAe | dGed B2 dg | dGeG BGAB | GEGA B2 Be |
dGeG BAAe | dGed B2 Ba | gfeg dgBG | EFGA BGAB |]

Other versions of this tune can be found here:
https://thesession.org/tunes/4652

The air was used apparently for a Gaelic song, “giving a ludicrous account of all the eccentricities of female dress.”

Re: Boil The Breakfast Early

On the name of the tune. We started integrating this into our local session here in Poitiers, France, and I thought I’d heard a story about the word ‘early’ in the title referring to Sergeant Early from Chicago, but I couldn’t remember where I’d heard it. This morning, I stumbled upon this introduction by Micho Russell, just a fun anecdote:
“Anyway, there was a man in Chicago by the name of Captain O’Neill. He was…, he was head of the police. So, he collected tunes all over America and Ireland. So, the story was that if [you had] the height and had a fair bit of education, you could become a sergeant who was there to play the music with Captain O’Neill. But anyways, he had a man called Sergeant Early. So he said to Early one morning “Boil the breakfast, Early.” So, I thought ‘twas boil it early in the morning, you see, but ‘twasn’t. His surname was Early. So, the name stuck to the tune ever since ‘Boil the Breakfast early’.”
Micho Russell, in Ireland’s Whistling Ambassador, track 17, recorded sometime between 1990 and 1993.
